    The 12-hour run produced a VALID demonstration reconstruction, a native hardware-constrained randomized simulator, nine proven/mastered primitive links, and a runnable PPO policy package. It did not solve the complete task to my own criteria: the preselected incumbent's final gate r0299 achieved 58/128 complete tasks and one hardware-violation episode, versus the recorded requirement of at least 80% and zero violations. Verification r0300 records a failed verdict. There is no official score or physical robot validation. What worked: a cupped starting pose retained/rested 127/128 independent raw releases without setup hardware violations. Analytic/optimized motion references plus learned PPO residuals gave reliable conditional toss/catch, recup and rolling skills. Refreshing handoff pools from actual predecessor endpoints exposed unsupported catches and repaired a real mismatch in training starts. A guarded first-recup transition improved the accepted whole-task policy without changing physics or silently dropping failures. The exported model and all 44 policy files match the evaluated sources, and standard-view final success/failure rollouts reproduce exactly. What failed: conditional mastery did not compose into robust complete execution within 18 s. Of 36 first-spin misses after a counted first catch, all met 270 deg active path, but 29 missed 70 deg opposed net and 8 exceeded 30 deg passive motion,with one overlap. Task-measured interval origins differed from controller-local progress. The later history feature captured impact rather than catch completion,with 57.61 deg median attitude error; I acknowledged that validation error and did not claim a reliable support observer. The development gain from an earlier final hold clock did not survive the paired acceptance gate. Short final PPO refinement did not meet its declared trigger and was discarded. Criteria text

Agent verification criteria, version3

These are my claims about my simulation, not an official evaluation. Version1 was declared before robot simulation or policy evaluation. Version2 added two explicit regrasp transitions. Version3 preserves those transitions and all motion,style,hardware,deadline and task-pass thresholds,and makes the human-placement protocol explicit after finding that requested release positions and resting equilibria differ. Reference: recorded reconstruction version3, r0017, frozen in research/reference_v3; TASK.md remains authoritative. Success must generalize to uncertain placement and physical properties while preserving the demonstrated manipulation method.

Evidence and interpretation

The ordered goal is: settle/capture the placed ball; toss and catch; turn it with fingers; toss and catch; turn it again; toss and catch; turn it again and continue holding. There is one ball and one right hand, with no environment support during the skill. Palm-up orientation, down-up launch pulses, opening fingers in flight, yielding catches and opposed thumb/finger rolling are demonstrated. The ball is never replaced or reset within an episode.

Clean flight intervals52–65,163–177,200–215 at30Hz last .433,.467,.500s; release/capture boundaries have about1frame uncertainty. Estimated upward speeds2.35,2.50,2.41m/s give rises .280,.319,.295m. Size/focal sensitivity gives .263–.340m. Long in-hand turn intervals78–151 (2.43s) and226–306 (2.67s) have about552°/544° accepted relative angular path, with incomplete texture tracking; exact full spin count is unobservable. The short turn186–199 (.43s) has about59° accepted relative path. Contiguous accepted local turns120–133,186–196,240–245 measure89.7°,28.1°,52.2° relative to the hand. Bootstrap sampling error is small, but method/hand-fit sensitivity warrants an inferred~10° allowance. Local anatomical-hand axes are recorded in analysis/rotation_evidence.json: mostly palm-normal for the first turn, mostly finger-longitudinal for the short turn, and largely thumb-side axis for the last. The large turns visibly change axes and include regrasps, not a prescribed single-axis revolution.

The anatomical palm tilt has median~32° and approximately18–50° main range. Long-turn medians~31° and35°. Wrist dips before launches span~.10–.19m; reconstructed wrist speed max1.11m/s and acceleration max15.33m/s². Long-finger PIP/DIP flexion decreases in flight: first hold-to-flight PIP changes about17°,22°,25° for index/middle/ring. Only the last307–314 frames (.233s) visibly settle; a longer final hold is required by the instruction, not claimed observed.

Monocular absolute depth is weak (propagated sigma median112mm); conditional silhouette uncertainty median20mm. Camera/scale errors are correlated. Absolute ball attitude and offsets across texture gaps are unknown. Criteria therefore use gravity, phase-relative motion and relative hand/object rotation, not absolute video coordinates or a final marked-ball attitude.

Deployment distribution and scope of the claim

The robot starting wrist and20finger positions are chosen once and recorded with the simulation. Human release positions cover independent ±15mm along and ±12mm across the usable palm region,with20%stress reaching ±25mm and ±20mm. Ball orientation is arbitrary. Height is the first nonpenetrating sphere–hand contact height at that lateral position,not a forced ball insertion. Human support lowers the ball over1.5s,holds.6s,and is then completely removed. No spring,torque,kinematic repositioning or other external object support acts after that release. The fixed hand pose must retain the ball through3s of unforced settling: no floor contact,the ball remains within.16m of the wrist and touches the hand at its end. Setup hardware limits apply throughout. Every sampled release is retained in the data;failed placements count as task failures and are never resampled.

At least95%of128fresh main-plus-stress human releases must satisfy this retention condition,with zero hardware violations,and at least95%must subsequently pass the independent1second supported-rest start test. The task episode begins after the fixed3s settling allowance,not after a variable wait for success. Report the released lateral coverage,the resting lateral coverage,the settling motions,and all rejected starts separately. The hand may funnel different released placements into the same cupped equilibrium;we do not claim a wide family of stationary equilibria or that the ball stays exactly where the human released it. This interpretation tests the user's varied placement directly,with a passive cup rather than artificial support. Task gates still draw the entire distribution,including releases that fail retention. The primitive start-pool restriction to independently valid starts is reported separately from whole-task performance.

Nominal ball radius33.5mm and mass57.7g are public-information priors. Main randomization covers radius32.7–34.3mm, mass56.0–59.4g, sliding friction0.45–1.1, and contact damping/stiffness around the reconstructed prior. Stress evaluation also covers radius31.5–35.5mm, mass50–65g and friction0.3–1.3. The exact distributions and contact parameter mapping must be recorded with the simulation and iteration, including the soft cover response, which the video does not measure. Every gate samples the full declared deployment distribution and fixed evaluator; report stress results separately as well as their contribution to the suite distribution. Sampled evaluation cannot prove literally every possible placement or real-world performance.

Quantities and shared rules

Use the real simulated state and actual contacts for judging, never commanded poses. Let H be the wrist frame, n=R_H*(0,1,0) the right-palm normal, f=R_H*(0,0,-1) the finger direction, and R_rel=R_H^T R_ball. Relative centre velocity removes wrist linear velocity and rotational transport. A held interval means actual hand contact with no environment contact. Opposed means held with thumb and at least one other finger touching. No reset, attachment, kinematic object force, or support outside the hand may help the policy. Any floor contact is failure. All finger position, velocity and applied-torque hardware rules must hold every physics tick; no episode with a hardware violation counts.

Episode deadline18s is an explicit robot execution allowance (~1.7× the10.5s demonstration) for adaptation, recovery and a longer final hold. It does not permit indefinitely holding on instead of completing the next stage.

All stages must preserve palm-up style: palm tilt10–65° for at least95% of manipulation time, never above80°; no wrist flip. Phase-mean anatomical wrist attitude, after a single fixed heading alignment to the chosen start, must remain within30° of the corresponding reference phase mean. This allowance combines approximately8° reconstruction uncertainty, natural adaptation and the different hand morphology; it is not to be tuned to a policy. Wrist speed must remain≤1.7m/s (1.11m/s observed, about50% allowance for reconstruction/retargeting and transients). Angular speed remains within hardware. Standard gate predicate wrist.max_rotation_deg≤65° rejects large wrist-driven turns. Object rotations must be relative to the wrist and actively driven by moving fingers.

Measure angular path as the sum of shortest frame-to-frame geodesic changes of R_rel, using a20ms sampling interval, only while held/opposed and excluding changes during free flight. To avoid counting noise, ignore changes below0.25° per20ms; also require substantial net motion within a single opposed interval. Fingers must move during rolling: passive_rel_rotation_deg is bounded as below. A sequence of wrist rotations or a loose ball slipping in a static grip is not a spin success.

Ordered stage completions

  1. settled: obtain at least .20s of continuous hand support, centre relative speed≤.08m/s and ball centre remaining inside the cupped hand; thumb/opposition may form during capture. Standard predicates held_s≥.20, touching_hand_at_end=1, environment_contact_s≤0.001. This entry prepares a genuine handoff for the first toss.
  2. catch1: exactly one completed toss/catch event after settled. Each toss must release into at least .30s without hand contact, rise .20–.40m above its own release height, have upward release speed1.9–2.9m/s, and return to hand support without floor contact. These bands surround .263–.340m sensitivity and the observed .43–.50s clean flights, with tolerance for contact boundaries and morphology. Before release the wrist makes a .05–.25m dip followed by upward motion, and at least two of the long-finger PIP/DIP chains open by mean≥.15rad relative to the prelaunch hold (the observed opening is about.3–.4rad for major PIPs). The open palm stays below the ball. A catch requires ≥.20s renewed support, relative centre speed≤.12m/s at completion and the ball within .14m of the palm centre; wrist gives downward by≥.015m around capture instead of meeting it with an upward strike. Standard predicates max_rise_m≥.20, held_s≥.20, environment_contact_s≤0.001. Own event judge checks release-relative rise and ordering; the global measurement alone does not establish a toss.
  3. spin1: while supported, finger-driven in-hand rolling achieves ≥270° cumulative relative angular path and ≥70° net change within one opposed interval. Maintain at least .30s opposed contact. This is below the incomplete552° estimate but requires several substantial turns rather than a token regrasp; gap/centre/model uncertainty prevents a precise revolution count. Axis changes/regra​​sps are allowed as observed. passive_rel_rotation_deg≤30°, with actual finger motion; wrist alone cannot satisfy this. Standard predicates opposed_s≥.30, opposed_rel_rotation_deg≥70°, passive_rel_rotation_deg≤30°, environment_contact_s≤0.001.
  4. ready2: after spin1 completes, restore a tossing cup while keeping the ball supported. Require a continuous .20s interval with actual hand support, relative centre speed≤.08m/s, finger positions within .15rad of the chosen initial cup, and ball centre within .025m of that cup's nominal centre in the wrist frame. No floor contact or hardware violation. These are the entry-support conditions plus an explicit cup handoff: .15rad is the independent start-check joint tolerance; .025m covers the declared placement spread (about.019m diagonal), radius variation and a few millimetres of contact/pose allowance. The video4.43–5.43s shows finger repositioning before the second launch; the robot needs a distinct transition because its long rolling controller ends with a shifted ball/grip. This is an added adaptation, not a claim that the human pauses this long. Standard predicates held_s≥.20,touching_hand_at_end=1,environment_contact_s≤.001,wrist.max_rotation_deg≤65.
  5. catch2: after spin1, complete the second toss/catch, with the same event/style rules as catch1. No extra toss may substitute for an in-hand turn.
  6. spin2: after catch2, achieve ≥30° cumulative held relative path and≥20° net change within one opposed interval, with at least .10s opposed contact and passive_rel_rotation_deg≤15°. The observed local28°±~10° and full short-phase59° support a distinct smaller turn; the threshold is not borrowed from the long turn. Standard predicates opposed_s≥.10, opposed_rel_rotation_deg≥20°, passive_rel_rotation_deg≤15°, environment_contact_s≤0.001.
  7. ready3: after spin2 completes, restore the same tossing cup under exactly the ready2 conditions, before the third toss. Video6.53–6.63s has a brief final finger adjustment before the next release; the robot may take longer within the unchanged18s deadline. This transition is included now because the same grip gap can recur. Standard predicates are identical to ready2.
  8. catch3: after spin2, complete the third toss/catch under the same event/style rules. There must be exactly three substantial toss/catch events by task completion.
  9. spin3_hold: after catch3, achieve ≥270° cumulative held relative path, ≥40° net change in one opposed interval and opposed_s≥.30, with passive_rel_rotation_deg≤30°. The observed local52° and incomplete544° phase path motivate these bounds. Then hold for a full1s, with hand support on≥95% of samples, opposed contact on≥80%, relative centre speed≤.05m/s, relative angular speed≤.5rad/s and centre displacement≤.015m throughout that final second. World ball speed≤.08m/s and angular speed≤.8rad/s rule out merely carrying/spinning it indefinitely. This extends the observed .233s ending to operationally meaningful continued holding, as TASK.md requires. Standard predicates touching_hand_at_end=1, touching_environment_at_end=0, last_second_max_speed_m_s≤.08, last_second_max_angular_speed_rad_s≤.8, opposed_rel_rotation_deg≥40°, passive_rel_rotation_deg≤30°, environment_contact_s≤0.001. The event judge checks the final rolling phase and1s stability separately.

The evaluator reports the nine stages only in order, plus diagnostics for each release, catch, roll and style violation. Each primitive suite uses only the criteria of its link and actual predecessor handoff states. Skill goal-relative orientations may be chosen to realize the measured local axis/angle; final ball attitude is not itself a task goal. Primitive reorientation specs use the recorded connected reference intervals, and their mandatory gate predicates remain in force. Long-turn task path criteria are additional to the local net-angle feasibility/skill tests.

Pass rate, evidence and ambiguity

Task success means all nine stages, every shared rule and all hardware rules hold in one uninterrupted episode. Required final task success rate: ≥0.80 on128fresh gate episodes, with zero hardware-violation episodes allowed. The rate is my declared threshold for a meaningful repeated manipulation skill over uncertain starts, not an official benchmark; report its Wilson interval and per-stage funnel rather than imply certainty. Development gates use at least32fresh episodes, broadened when needed; final selection uses development results only. Each learned primitive must meet≥0.80 from its handoff distribution before whole-task PPO training. Feasibility controllers require≥0.25 but should be improved toward≥0.90 before distillation/training.

All successes/failures are supported by complete state logs, independent standard measurements, standard top/left/right videos and viewed gate montages. Final verdict must name its final gate and iteration. A controller/reference baseline is not a learned policy. The verified final policy is PPO-trained and observes only permitted state/history; it never observes contacts, forces, physical parameters, rewards or images. If a criterion proves physically incompatible with the specified hardware, record the calculation and evidence before any separately versioned revision; never lower it simply to pass a policy.

Open issues are stated rather than filled with invented evidence: exact ball revolutions, hidden fingertip contacts, absolute monocular depth, material coefficients and long-duration real-world holding are unresolved by this one video. The simulation and stress tests must address them, and its verdict will remain a simulation-only claim.

Reason for version2

The first rolling feasibility controller r0051 changes the grip and ball centre. Three attempts to reuse or repair the next toss (r0055,r0059,r0060) missed catches, and some violated hardware limits. The chain therefore needs explicit supported regrasp transitions, as LEARNING/VERIFICATION require for a gap between links. The two new stages make the requirements stricter; no existing threshold is relaxed. Earlier criteria1 and suite versions remain in the record. A separate evaluator correction recognizes catch completion at any subsequent continuous .20s supported interval satisfying the original speed threshold, rather than incorrectly requiring the first .20s immediately after impact. That correction was documented at r0036; it does not waive contact, speed, flight or ordering requirements. Final claims under version2 use new suites and will not relabel earlier results.

Reason for version3

The earlier placement generator held the ball with a fading3s spring before unforced settling. Measured requested positions spanned about38mm×48mm,but actual rest positions only2.0mm×0.9mm(r0087). A broad-actual-rest interpretation would therefore be unsupported. Raw-release geometry tests across45palm/platform/cup variants found that a ball released on a curved surface often rolls more than20degrees before resting,even while safely retained. The chosen cup retained all32main releases in several candidates;the full-distribution check then retained127/128fresh releases,127/128passed the rest check,and zero violated hardware. The failed release31105 remains a failure. Version3 replaces ambiguous broad stationary placement with explicit broad release coverage plus a separately tested passive retention process. This changes the initial-condition claim rather than relabelling earlier narrow-pool results. It removes the fading support spring;all postrelease settling is physical. It does not lower any manipulation threshold or the80%task requirement. Final claims must use the revised generator and report the remaining physical-model uncertainty.

Before release the wrist makes a .05–.25m dip followed by upward motion, and at least two of the long-finger PIP/DIP chains open by mean≥.15rad relative to the prelaunch hold (the observed opening is about.3–.4rad for major PIPs). The open palm stays below the ball. A catch requires ≥.20s renewed support, relative centre speed≤.12m/s at completion and the ball within .14m of the palm centre; wrist gives downward by≥.015m around capture instead of meeting it with an upward strike. Standard predicates max_rise_m≥.20, held_s≥.20, environment_contact_s≤0.001. Own event judge checks release-relative rise and ordering; the global measurement alone does not establish a toss.
  3. spin1: while supported, finger-driven in-hand rolling achieves ≥270° cumulative relative angular path and ≥70° net change within one opposed interval. Maintain at least .30s opposed contact. This is below the incomplete552° estimate but requires several substantial turns rather than a token regrasp; gap/centre/model uncertainty prevents a precise revolution count. Axis changes/regra​​sps are allowed as observed. passive_rel_rotation_deg≤30°, with actual finger motion; wrist alone cannot satisfy this. Standard predicates opposed_s≥.30, opposed_rel_rotation_deg≥70°, passive_rel_rotation_deg≤30°, environment_contact_s≤0.001.
  4. ready2: after spin1 completes, restore a tossing cup while keeping the ball supported. Require a continuous .20s interval with actual hand support, relative centre speed≤.08m/s, finger positions within .15rad of the chosen initial cup, and ball centre within .025m of that cup's nominal centre in the wrist frame. No floor contact or hardware violation. These are the entry-support conditions plus an explicit cup handoff: .15rad is the independent start-check joint tolerance; .025m covers the declared placement spread (about.019m diagonal), radius variation and a few millimetres of contact/pose allowance. The video4.43–5.43s shows finger repositioning before the second launch; the robot needs a distinct transition because its long rolling controller ends with a shifted ball/grip. This is an added adaptation, not a claim that the human pauses this long. Standard predicates held_s≥.20,touching_hand_at_end=1,environment_contact_s≤.001,wrist.max_rotation_deg≤65.
  5. catch2: after spin1, complete the second toss/catch, with the same event/style rules as catch1. No extra toss may substitute for an in-hand turn.
  6. spin2: after catch2, achieve ≥30° cumulative held relative path and≥20° net change within one opposed interval, with at least .10s opposed contact and passive_rel_rotation_deg≤15°. The observed local28°±~10° and full short-phase59° support a distinct smaller turn; the threshold is not borrowed from the long turn. Standard predicates opposed_s≥.10, opposed_rel_rotation_deg≥20°, passive_rel_rotation_deg≤15°, environment_contact_s≤0.001.
  7. ready3: after spin2 completes, restore the same tossing cup under exactly the ready2 conditions, before the third toss. Video6.53–6.63s has a brief final finger adjustment before the next release; the robot may take longer within the unchanged18s deadline. This transition is included now because the same grip gap can recur. Standard predicates are identical to ready2.
  8. catch3: after spin2, complete the third toss/catch under the same event/style rules. There must be exactly three substantial toss/catch events by task completion.
  9. spin3_hold: after catch3, achieve ≥270° cumulative held relative path, ≥40° net change in one opposed interval and opposed_s≥.30, with passive_rel_rotation_deg≤30°. The observed local52° and incomplete544° phase path motivate these bounds. Then hold for a full1s, with hand support on≥95% of samples, opposed contact on≥80%, relative centre speed≤.05m/s, relative angular speed≤.5rad/s and centre displacement≤.015m throughout that final second. World ball speed≤.08m/s and angular speed≤.8rad/s rule out merely carrying/spinning it indefinitely. This extends the observed .233s ending to operationally meaningful continued holding, as TASK.md requires. Standard predicates touching_hand_at_end=1, touching_environment_at_end=0, last_second_max_speed_m_s≤.08, last_second_max_angular_speed_rad_s≤.8, opposed_rel_rotation_deg≥40°, passive_rel_rotation_deg≤30°, environment_contact_s≤0.001. The event judge checks the final rolling phase and1s stability separately.

The evaluator reports the nine stages only in order, plus diagnostics for each release, catch, roll and style violation. Each primitive suite uses only the criteria of its link and actual predecessor handoff states. Skill goal-relative orientations may be chosen to realize the measured local axis/angle; final ball attitude is not itself a task goal. Primitive reorientation specs use the recorded connected reference intervals, and their mandatory gate predicates remain in force. Long-turn task path criteria are additional to the local net-angle feasibility/skill tests.

Pass rate, evidence and ambiguity

Task success means all nine stages, every shared rule and all hardware rules hold in one uninterrupted episode. Required final task success rate: ≥0.80 on128fresh gate episodes, with zero hardware-violation episodes allowed. The rate is my declared threshold for a meaningful repeated manipulation skill over uncertain starts, not an official benchmark; report its Wilson interval and per-stage funnel rather than imply certainty. Development gates use at least32fresh episodes, broadened when needed; final selection uses development results only. Each learned primitive must meet≥0.80 from its handoff distribution before whole-task PPO training. Feasibility controllers require≥0.25 but should be improved toward≥0.90 before distillation/training.

All successes/failures are supported by complete state logs, independent standard measurements, standard top/left/right videos and viewed gate montages. Final verdict must name its final gate and iteration. A controller/reference baseline is not a learned policy. The verified final policy is PPO-trained and observes only permitted state/history; it never observes contacts, forces, physical parameters, rewards or images. If a criterion proves physically incompatible with the specified hardware, record the calculation and evidence before any separately versioned revision; never lower it simply to pass a policy.

Open issues are stated rather than filled with invented evidence: exact ball revolutions, hidden fingertip contacts, absolute monocular depth, material coefficients and long-duration real-world holding are unresolved by this one video. The simulation and stress tests must address them, and its verdict will remain a simulation-only claim.

Reason for version2

The first rolling feasibility controller r0051 changes the grip and ball centre. Three attempts to reuse or repair the next toss (r0055,r0059,r0060) missed catches, and some violated hardware limits. The chain therefore needs explicit supported regrasp transitions, as LEARNING/VERIFICATION require for a gap between links. The two new stages make the requirements stricter; no existing threshold is relaxed. Earlier criteria1 and suite versions remain in the record. A separate evaluator correction recognizes catch completion at any subsequent continuous .20s supported interval satisfying the original speed threshold, rather than incorrectly requiring the first .20s immediately after impact. That correction was documented at r0036; it does not waive contact, speed, flight or ordering requirements. Final claims under version2 use new suites and will not relabel earlier results.

Criteria text

Agent verification criteria, version1

These are my claims about my simulation, not an official evaluation. They are declared before robot simulation or policy evaluation. Reference: recorded reconstruction version3, r0017, frozen in research/reference_v3; TASK.md remains authoritative. Success must generalize to uncertain placement and physical properties while preserving the demonstrated manipulation method.

Evidence and interpretation

The ordered goal is: settle/capture the placed ball; toss and catch; turn it with fingers; toss and catch; turn it again; toss and catch; turn it again and continue holding. There is one ball and one right hand, with no environment support during the skill. Palm-up orientation, down-up launch pulses, opening fingers in flight, yielding catches and opposed thumb/finger rolling are demonstrated. The ball is never replaced or reset within an episode.

Clean flight intervals52–65,163–177,200–215 at30Hz last .433,.467,.500s; release/capture boundaries have about1frame uncertainty. Estimated upward speeds2.35,2.50,2.41m/s give rises .280,.319,.295m. Size/focal sensitivity gives .263–.340m. Long in-hand turn intervals78–151 (2.43s) and226–306 (2.67s) have about552°/544° accepted relative angular path, with incomplete texture tracking; exact full spin count is unobservable. The short turn186–199 (.43s) has about59° accepted relative path. Contiguous accepted local turns120–133,186–196,240–245 measure89.7°,28.1°,52.2° relative to the hand. Bootstrap sampling error is small, but method/hand-fit sensitivity warrants an inferred~10° allowance. Local anatomical-hand axes are recorded in analysis/rotation_evidence.json: mostly palm-normal for the first turn, mostly finger-longitudinal for the short turn, and largely thumb-side axis for the last. The large turns visibly change axes and include regrasps, not a prescribed single-axis revolution.

The anatomical palm tilt has median~32° and approximately18–50° main range. Long-turn medians~31° and35°. Wrist dips before launches span~.10–.19m; reconstructed wrist speed max1.11m/s and acceleration max15.33m/s². Long-finger PIP/DIP flexion decreases in flight: first hold-to-flight PIP changes about17°,22°,25° for index/middle/ring. Only the last307–314 frames (.233s) visibly settle; a longer final hold is required by the instruction, not claimed observed.

Monocular absolute depth is weak (propagated sigma median112mm); conditional silhouette uncertainty median20mm. Camera/scale errors are correlated. Absolute ball attitude and offsets across texture gaps are unknown. Criteria therefore use gravity, phase-relative motion and relative hand/object rotation, not absolute video coordinates or a final marked-ball attitude.

Deployment distribution and scope of the claim

The robot starting wrist and20finger positions are chosen once and recorded with the simulation. The ball is placed roughly in the palm centre with independent horizontal displacement covering at least ±15mm along and ±12mm across the usable palm region, with a broader stress set reaching ±25mm and ±20mm. Ball orientation is arbitrary. The start distribution is not restricted to the demonstration placement. Starts are physically at rest and hand-supported, checked by the independent1second hold-policy start test. Do not discard falling placements to improve evaluation: report the tested placement support and start-check failures, and adjust the starting hand pose if needed.

Nominal ball radius33.5mm and mass57.7g are public-information priors. Main randomization covers radius32.7–34.3mm, mass56.0–59.4g, sliding friction0.45–1.1, and contact damping/stiffness around the reconstructed prior. Stress evaluation also covers radius31.5–35.5mm, mass50–65g and friction0.3–1.3. The exact distributions and contact parameter mapping must be recorded with the simulation and iteration, including the soft cover response, which the video does not measure. Every gate samples the full declared deployment distribution and fixed evaluator; report stress results separately as well as their contribution to the suite distribution. Sampled evaluation cannot prove literally every possible placement or real-world performance.

Quantities and shared rules

Use the real simulated state and actual contacts for judging, never commanded poses. Let H be the wrist frame, n=R_H*(0,1,0) the right-palm normal, f=R_H*(0,0,-1) the finger direction, and R_rel=R_H^T R_ball. Relative centre velocity removes wrist linear velocity and rotational transport. A held interval means actual hand contact with no environment contact. Opposed means held with thumb and at least one other finger touching. No reset, attachment, kinematic object force, or support outside the hand may help the policy. Any floor contact is failure. All finger position, velocity and applied-torque hardware rules must hold every physics tick; no episode with a hardware violation counts.

Episode deadline18s is an explicit robot execution allowance (~1.7× the10.5s demonstration) for adaptation, recovery and a longer final hold. It does not permit indefinitely holding on instead of completing the next stage.

All stages must preserve palm-up style: palm tilt10–65° for at least95% of manipulation time, never above80°; no wrist flip. Phase-mean anatomical wrist attitude, after a single fixed heading alignment to the chosen start, must remain within30° of the corresponding reference phase mean. This allowance combines approximately8° reconstruction uncertainty, natural adaptation and the different hand morphology; it is not to be tuned to a policy. Wrist speed must remain≤1.7m/s (1.11m/s observed, about50% allowance for reconstruction/retargeting and transients). Angular speed remains within hardware. Standard gate predicate wrist.max_rotation_deg≤65° rejects large wrist-driven turns. Object rotations must be relative to the wrist and actively driven by moving fingers.

Measure angular path as the sum of shortest frame-to-frame geodesic changes of R_rel, using a20ms sampling interval, only while held/opposed and excluding changes during free flight. To avoid counting noise, ignore changes below0.25° per20ms; also require substantial net motion within a single opposed interval. Fingers must move during rolling: passive_rel_rotation_deg is bounded as below. A sequence of wrist rotations or a loose ball slipping in a static grip is not a spin success.

  4. catch2: after spin1, complete the second toss/catch, with the same event/style rules as catch1. No extra toss may substitute for an in-hand turn.
  5. spin2: after catch2, achieve ≥30° cumulative held relative path and≥20° net change within one opposed interval, with at least .10s opposed contact and passive_rel_rotation_deg≤15°. The observed local28°±~10° and full short-phase59° support a distinct smaller turn; the threshold is not borrowed from the long turn. reflectionThe 12-hour run produced a VALID demonstration reconstruction, a native hardware-constrained randomized simulator, nine proven/mastered primitive links, and a runnable PPO policy package. It did not…
more
The 12-hour run produced a VALID demonstration reconstruction, a native hardware-constrained randomized simulator, nine proven/mastered primitive links, and a runnable PPO policy package. It did not solve the complete task to my own criteria: the preselected incumbent's final gate r0299 achieved 58/128 complete tasks and one hardware-violation episode, versus the recorded requirement of at least 80% and zero violations. Verification r0300 records a failed verdict. There is no official score or physical robot validation. What worked: a cupped starting pose retained/rested 127/128 independent raw releases without setup hardware violations. Analytic/optimized motion references plus learned PPO residuals gave reliable conditional toss/catch, recup and rolling skills. Refreshing handoff pools from actual predecessor endpoints exposed unsupported catches and repaired a real mismatch in training starts. A guarded first-recup transition improved the accepted whole-task policy without changing physics or silently dropping failures. The exported model and all 44 policy files match the evaluated sources, and standard-view final success/failure rollouts reproduce exactly. What failed: conditional mastery did not compose into robust complete execution within 18 s. Of 36 first-spin misses after a counted first catch, all met 270 deg active path, but 29 missed 70 deg opposed net and 8 exceeded 30 deg passive motion,with one overlap. Task-measured interval origins differed from controller-local progress. The later history feature captured impact rather than catch completion,with 57.61 deg median attitude error; I acknowledged that validation error and did not claim a reliable support observer. The development gain from an earlier final hold clock did not survive the paired acceptance gate. Short final PPO refinement did not meet its declared trigger and was discarded. Post-selection diagnosis localized the remaining failures without replacing the policy. All 11 final-hold misse…
 · r0306 · Nov 15, 10:05 EST

Last-budget descriptive parameter audit of the unchanged final policy: regenerated the frozen RNG physical draws and validated all six against reproduced stress1842615469. In the main distribution,friction below0.5 had0/9 complete tasks (1/9 first-spin passes),0.5–0.7 had8/27,0.7–0.9 had29/37,and0.9–1.1 had17/29. These are post-hoc associations with small bins,not causal interventions or an allowed narrowing of the deployment distribution. All128 trials stay in the final58/128 denominator. This supports prioritizing low-friction opposing support while retaining the full stress envelope. CSV and exact groups:research/final_parameter_trials.csv,research/final_parameter_associations.json. No parameters were fed to the actor and no policy/criteria changed.
